note.title: Finite verb control
note.overview: This note supports 7 source-backed questions on Finite verb control.
mustMemoriseRules: Find and check the verb before deciding the noun cases.

workedExamples.why: laborat is the finite verb; it controls the sentence “the slave works”.
dormit is the finite verb; it controls the sentence “the dog sleeps”.
portat is the finite verb; it controls the sentence “the slave carries the dog”.
dat is the finite verb; it controls the sentence “the slave gives a letter to the brother”.
ambulat is the finite verb; it controls the sentence “he/she walks to the garden”.

commonMistakes: Recognising the meaning but submitting an incomplete form or spelling.

A familiar Latin form is recognised but translated too vaguely.
detailedExplanation: This note supports 7 source-backed questions on Finite verb control.

A Latin verb form combines stem, tense information and a personal ending. Work from the ending inward: identify person and number, then tense or mood, then translate with the correct time relationship.
examTips: Mark the finite verb first, then use noun endings to assign subject, object and recipient roles.
Normal Latin word order can vary; the case, number, gender, person and tense endings cannot.
For English to Latin, build each required form before arranging the sentence.
